Home
Bede's is an independent, co-educational school located on two stunning sites, one by the sea in Eastbourne and one in the heart of the Sussex countryside, offering education from 3 months to 18 years.
Do what you love.
Merit or above at BTEC
2025 Sixth Form pupils got their first choice places at university
Pupils at Bede’s School in Sussex are celebrating today after delivering another record-breaking performance, securing the school’s best-ever GCSE results. Just under half (47%) of all grades awarded were at the highest 9–7 level (or equivalent).
Pupils at Bede’s School are celebrating a historic academic milestone today, having achieved the finest A Level and BTEC results in the Sussex school’s history. An impressive 84% of all grades were awarded at A* to B, with a third of all grades (33%) achieved at the top A* level (or equivalent).
Bede’s School is delighted to announce a prestigious new commercial partnership with Premier League club Brighton & Hove Albion FC. This collaboration unites two of the South East’s leading institutions, establishing a strong partnership alignment rooted in shared values, community engagement and focus on developing excellence.
Academic Values
2025 Results

Partnerships
At the very heart of the Bede’s partnership programme is the importance of fostering a caring community which not only exists within our own school environment, but also reaches those in the local community and beyond.
By working alongside people from various parts of our community, we believe our students develop social virtues that allow them to better understand and make a positive contribution to wider society.
The benefit of being able to share our facilities, talents, time and expertise is hugely important, whilst at the same time recognising that each Bedian will learn as much if not more from our partners as they do.
We aim for all our pupils:
- To be ready and willing to make a positive contribution to the wider community and environment - To develop elements of their own character, fostering the four main schools values to be:
- To appreciate the privileges they have and understand the duty they have to make the world a better place - To develop skills, knowledge and creativity to serve groups and communities with whom they partner
I am thrilled to be able to showcase how our students have been making an impact amongst the local and wider community.
Partnership Participation
The focus on partnerships runs through every aspect of school life at Bede’s and is developed through the academic curriculum, the co-curricular programme as well as through the pastoral system. All partnership activities are designed to be sustainable, long term and to deliver mutual benefit to all recipients.
Wealden Partnership
Educational Facilities
Academic Performance
LAC & other organisations
Wealden Partnership (WSP)
The Wealden Partnership (WSP) is constituted as a partnership of equals amongst 10 primary and secondary schools in the Wealden area. The shared aim is the educational benefit of children based on a core belief that children in the Wealden area will be better served through cooperation and a recognition of the similarities of our objectives. In the past year, we have organised all sorts of activities and events from inter house debating competitions, quizzes, sport and coaching sessions, school council get togethers as well as SHAPE, STEM and language days across the schools.
Educational Facilities
Facilities across both schools continue to be used extensively by local organisations, schools and communities. All drama performances offer free places for local school children whether at the Devonshire Park and Congress theatres or in house productions. This is an opportunity which sparks children’s own creativity and their interest in the performing arts.
Various schools have been able to use our recording studios whilst other schools have forged links with our chapel and concert choirs. Free places have been awarded to the Legat programme, as well as the summer school dance programme and national let’s dance competition. The summer school offers free places to refugees and under privileged children.
Numerous schools visit the school zoo offering a hands-on experience as well as looking at care and conservation.
Academic Performance
Building upon last year's connection with Gladesmore, this year we joined forces again alongside Elmgreen school. STEM pupils and teachers are able to offer 2 hour online teaching every Monday after school to gifted Year 10 pupils from both schools. They were delighted that they were able to make a visit to Bede’s in April, taking part in bespoke science and maths lessons including practical sessions as well as a much enjoyed trip to the zoo.
Andrine Allen from AA Educates said “On behalf of the students and staff, I would like to say a HUGE thank you for ALL your hospitality and your warm welcome. As usual, the staff and students at Bede's were friendly, warm and very helpful.
The pupils reported how much they enjoyed their experience and got so much from the day. Thank you for hosting the STEM workshops and amazing practical experiments as well as the online tuition. Thank you for your continued generosity and support and keeping this partnership flourishing”
"I enjoyed my trip to Bede’s. I like that they have a lot of different subjects and activities they can do in and out of school. I like the way the school promotes inclusivity and how they were welcoming”
In January, we hold the Senior Inter Schools debating competition. Five different schools in the area joined together for a debating experience led by Head of Languages, Matthew Oliver. MP Nusrat Ghani introduced the morning via a zoom call, where she highlighted how events like this help to develop critical thinking skills, showing respect to others, gaining understanding as well as providing challenge and persuasion for the different points of view. The format of the morning was explained, before the motions were discussed. The two motions were “should foreign aid be dissolved?” and “should the consumption of meat be banned?” Feedback was given to all students with books given out to those that gave a particularly impressive performance. A huge thank you to our pupils that participated but also to all schools involved for their commitment and support.
A member of staff within the STEM Faculty fulfils the role of CEO of the Galactic Challenge Enterprise and plays a significant role in organising annual events. We were able to host academic enrichment days for local primary schools as well as continuing to organise and host the Galactic Challenge and the UK Space Design Competition in November and March. The School organised and ran the regional round of the UK Space Design Challenge on behalf of the educational charity Space Science Engineering Foundation (SSEF). Over 200 pupils were involved in these events. We were once again able to host a primary STEM schools fair for 8-10 other schools to showcase their work. The faculty held a ‘Mission to Mars’ day for local primary schools in an attempt to encourage children into STEM and space education in particular.
The SHAPE faculty visited five different schools delivering a variety of workshops entitled ‘cities from scratch,’ as well as ‘starting your own business day.’ The SHAPE faculty also organised the MUN conference for five local schools as well as hosting the European Youth Parliament South Coast Regional Finals. They also delivered a mini debating workshop at two local schools.
The school library organised for the schools reading ambassadors to read with Year 3 and Year 4 students at Parkmead. This was a fantastic opportunity to encourage the love of reading beyond school boundaries.
In April the Head of Careers organised a careers fayre with over 100 exhibitors from local and national employers as well as universities and apprenticeships. 350 Children from four local schools were able to attend and explore the next stage of their careers.
LAC & Other Organisations
A member of staff at Bede’s continues his long-standing commitment and support of Looked After Children (LAC) by acting as the Designated Teacher for LACs. Bede’s works closely with the RNCSF and our Designated Teacher is a member of their Expert Advisory Group, providing advice about boarding, in order to help develop their national programme. During the past year, there were five LAC from East Sussex who were educated in the Trust, all of whom were weekly boarding at Bede’s. The School also supported one child from Eastside Young Leaders’ Academy (EYLA), through the Royal National Children’s SpringBoard Foundation (RNCSF). The School provides 50% bursaries for the LAC and also covers many of the extra costs, with the Local Authority and the Royal National Children’s SpringBoard Foundation providing the remainder of fees. Bede’s also provides a 70% bursary for the child from EYLA, with the RNCSF covering the rest including extras.
Our Designated Teacher for LAC has also continued to fulfil his role as a Governor of the East Sussex Virtual School for Children in Care, with the school hosting two of the Governor meetings this year. In this role, he also works closely with the Head of the Virtual School to identify children in care who would benefit from a place at Bede’s and to explore ways in which Bede’s can support and provide opportunities to other children in care in East Sussex.
The Head of LAC has also developed a partnership with Magdalen College School in Oxford offering interview and mock Oxbridge Maths support for a variety of students in state schools.
As part of its work to support the Foster Placement Support Service, which provides respite for foster carers, Bede’s hosts children several times a year at weekends and during holidays. Every term we hosted groups of up to 15 children on a Saturday morning, providing activities in both the Art and Animal Management Unit and providing lunch. On two occasions we hosted two groups of LAC for holiday sports activities, led by staff in the Sports Centre, during which they tried out a number of different sports.
We hosted two Children in Care Awards ceremonies this year. In October, we hosted over 50 children in care along with their carers/ social workers to celebrate their educational success. Holroyd Howe provided the catering and the awards ceremony took place in the Recital room. This event was for children in Year 7 and above. In March, we held an event to celebrate the educational success of such children in Year 6 and below. 20 children along with their carers, were invited in for a session in art and animal management, followed by lunch and the award ceremony in the Old Dining Room.
Last year Bede’s was recognised for its work with LAC over the course of the last decade, by the Boarding Schools Association, winning the Working with Vulnerable Children Award. The award submission detailed research carried out by Bede’s Head of Boarding into the experience of and outcomes for LAC who have attended Bede’s. The evidence provided explained that to date 22 LAC have attended Bede’s and that, whilst some are still currently studying at Bede’s, 14 children have left with the equivalent of 3 A levels or more and a university offer, the vast majority having achieved considerable academic success at university.
We continue to have links with Sibs, a national charity supporting children who have disabled siblings or parents. As a result, we work with Downs Junior School in Brighton, which is the only primary school in the South East to have a Sibs group. Across two Saturdays, groups of up to 12 children came in for sessions in Art and Animal Management followed by lunch. Transport to and from Brighton was provided on both occasions.
Social Responsibility
Community Relations
Local Charity Work & Volunteering
Co-curricular Performance
Sharing Knowledge
Community Relations
The Senior School values highly its role within the local village community of Upper Dicker and its environs. We continue to support Christmas Carol singing in the village, donating money towards the cost of the evening including food, decorations and presents as well as supporting the event itself with pupils and staff. This event is a fantastic social gathering for everyone that resides in the village. The School also plays a significant role helping with the organisation of Dicker Day which is an event organised in the Village by local residents.
The School maintains services to the village church, including undertaking repairs and tending to the graveyards, cutting hedges, as well as other village amenities, tending to the football pitch and verges. Our car park continues to be used for large events at the village church and daily by the parents of the village primary school for drop off and pick up. During the winter months, the School grits the paths in the village, especially around Park Mead Primary School.
Local residents are able to use the School’s swimming pool and have access to the gym at certain times of the week, all of which are free. Bede’s also provides emergency support within the village from time to time, for example by providing water to the primary school on occasions when the water supply to the village has been cut off for prolonged periods. The School prints and supplies ID cards for Park Mead School
Senior pupils provide reading support to all age groups at Parkmead, building strong relationships with the children and volunteer at events such as the Christmas fayre and sports day. Food was also provided for these events from the Food and Nutrition department.
Local Charity Work & Volunteering
Pupils at Bede’s are encouraged to develop their relationship with the wider community, through the charitable actions of giving to others, whether that be their time, energy or financial contributions. They are encouraged to develop a strong sense of civic duty and a clear understanding of the values of charitable fundraising and volunteering.
This year Bede's has continued to foster their link with the Matthew 25 Mission in Eastbourne. A charity which cares for vulnerable people who have been exploited and downtrodden. In the Autumn term, as part of the traditional October Harvest Festival, Bede’s school was able to donate enough dry food to provide 2,000 meals. The donation drive fostered an awareness towards the struggles of those in our own community and helped to encourage a sense of compassion and curiosity.
At Christmas, 150 love in a bag parcels were filled with gifts and donated to Hailsham Food bank which were then distributed to families who would not otherwise be able to afford it.
At Easter, 450 easter eggs were donated to The Recovery cafe and psychiatric clinic in Hellingly.. This charity seeks to support anyone on a recovery journey. Residents were overwhelmed when they realised other people were thinking of them.
We were able to host the Demelza Bubble Run in the summer term including all the set up, equipment loan, grounds and facilities.
The Prep School runs a weekly activity called Young at Heart during which a group of pupils visit care homes to spend time engagin

Years 10 & 11
Years 10 and 11 mark an exciting milestone where pupils shape their studies around their academic interests and passions.
As you move into Years 10 and 11, you will reach some of the most important and rewarding stages of your school journey. This is an exciting time to start focusing on the subjects that match your interests, strengths, and future aspirations.
We do not wait for opportunities. We create them.
Alongside the vital core subjects of English, Maths and Science, you will have the chance to select from a rich variety of GCSE and BTEC options, ranging from deep academic rigour to creative and practical applications.
Of course, you won't have to navigate these choices alone; our dedicated tutors, Heads of Departments and the Careers team are on hand every step of the way to help each pupil design their own bespoke timetable.
Making the Most of Your Time at Bede’s
On this Bede’s journey, we encourage our pupils to view their education as a true adventure. We offer a range of subjects, activities and experiences, helping you explore incredible possibilities, both within the academic curriculum and through our wider enrichment options. For every pathway chosen, we will support our learners to push academic boundaries, step outside their comfort zones to embrace fresh ideas, and surpass their own expectations.
Within our supportive environment, you will find the confidence to transform seemingly insurmountable challenges into fascinating discoveries, using a wonderful blend of curiosity, creativity and an open mind
Exploring Opportunities
The Upper School offers much more than academic study alone. Through our broad curriculum and extensive co-curricular programme, you will have opportunities to develop new skills, discover new interests and gain experiences that will help shape your future. We hope you will approach these opportunities with curiosity and a willingness to step outside your comfort zone.
Pastoral Support and Wellbeing
Your wellbeing and personal development remain at the heart of what we do. Our pastoral team is here to support you throughout these important years, whether you need help with academic decisions, co-curricular commitments, or the day-to-day challenges of school life. We want every pupil to feel valued, supported and able to thrive within our community.
Looking Ahead
As you progress through Years 10 and 11, you will develop the knowledge, skills and resilience needed for the next stage of your education. We hope you will discover new strengths, build lasting friendships, and gain the confidence to pursue your ambitions. We look forward to supporting you throughout this journey and celebrating your achievements along the way.

Years 7 to 9
From September 2027, Years 7 and 8 will move from our Prep School to form the junior years within our new Upper School at Eastbourne, offering a seamless transition through to the GCSE year groups of 10 an 11.
We ask better questions than yesterday.
Why These Years Matter
Years 7 to 9 in the UK, collectively known as Key Stage 3, mark the vital transition from primary school to secondary education. Typically covering ages 11 to 14, these years are far more than just a bridge to GCSEs; they are a critical formative period for academic and personal growth.
Academic Breadth:
KS3 offers the most diverse curriculum a student will encounter. Pupils explore a wide array of subjects - from the sciences and humanities to modern languages and the arts - before narrowing their focus for exam courses.
Skill Development:
This stage builds the foundational critical thinking, independent study habits and analytical skills required for future academic success.
Personal Growth:
The Upper School environment encourages pupils to develop independence, resilience and social development.
Ultimately, Years 7 to 9 provide the essential safety net where students can experiment, discover their strengths, and build the confidence needed to make informed choices about their GCSE options. It is during these years that the mindset for lifelong learning is truly forged.
Join us for our upcoming open morning
Explore everything Bede’s has to offer at our next Open Morning. Register your place today.

Pastoral Care
Bede’s has long been renowned for the quality of its pastoral care. Our Upper School will follow the same successful model as our Prep School, with the Form Teachers taking the lead on pastoral care which acts as a safety net built into daily school life.
At Bede’s, wellbeing and ambition thrive side by side.
Emotional & Mental Health Support
Social Well-being & Behavior
Safeguarding & Physical Safety
Personal Development & Life Skills
The school day begins at 8.25am for all pupils with some opting to join our breakfast club. Many children come in on the school bus service from across the county and some may opt to take the train to Eastbourne.
The day finishes for pupils around 4pm and then a little later at 5.20pm as pupils move through the school and take advantage of the activities offered. Late stay through to 6pm is also offered.

Board of Governors
To write to the Board of Governors, please address correspondence to:
Nicholas Mercer Chair of the Board of Governors c/o Clerk to the Board Bede's Senior School Upper Dicker East Sussex, BN27 3QH
Bede’s School in Upper Dicker, East Sussex was awarded ‘School of the Year’ at The Association of Governing Bodies of Independent Schools (AGBIS) annual conference in London on 18 March.
The Board of Governors have been awarded the 2023-24 Good Governance Programme certificate. This Programme was jointly developed by the Association of Governing Bodies in Independent Schools (AGBIS) and Headmasters' and Headmistresses' Conference (HMC) to support and provide recognition of high-quality governance in schools. It requires all Governors to undertake additional Safeguarding training and alongside taking part in training on a wide variety of relevant topics. The certificate will remain valid for three years.
Bede’s is an independent co-educational day and boarding School located on three sites. We offer education from the age of 3 months through to 18 years old through our Nursery, Prep School and Upper School based in Eastbourne and Lower School, Senior School and Sixth Form based at Upper Dicker. We also offer education for girls only aged 4 – 18 years old at Burgess Hill Girls. We also run a Summer School at various campuses.
About the Governors
St Bede's School Trust Sussex is a company limited by guarantee where the members of the Board of Governors are also the Directors and Members of the Company. As the Trust is a registered charity, the members of the Board of Governors are also Trustees of the Charity. The Trust runs on a not-for-profit basis, whereby any surplus generated is used to further the charitable objects. Governors are all volunteers and do not benefit financially from their involvement with the Trust.
The Board of Governors is responsible for planning the strategic direction of the whole Trust, which is then implemented by the Executive Leadership Team. The Board of Governors is also required to confirm that the Trust is compliant with all relevant legislation and operates as a going concern.
The Board of Governors meets approximately four times a year with a number of sub-committees meeting three times a year prior to each main Board meeting. The Governors have overall responsibility for maintaining oversight of safeguarding and ensuring that appropriate consideration is given to the need to eliminate unlawful discrimination, advance equality of opportunity and foster inclusion. The key current sub-committees, with their key responsibilities, are shown below:
Audit and Risk Committee:
a) Monitoring and reviewing systems and methods of risk control through the Risk Register including risk identification, risk analysis, emerging risks, and risk management.
b) Responsibility for the oversight of internal audit and the implementation of appropriate controls.
Education Committee:
a) Monitoring and reviewing the agreed academic, curricular, and pastoral provision of the Trust and making recommendations to the Board as appropriate.
b) Maintaining oversight of ‘safeguarding’ as this pertains to the Trust’s delivery of academic, curricular, and pastoral provision.
Finance Committee:
a) Overseeing all financial aspects of the Trust including annual budgeting and the setting of fees to ensure the Trust’s viability and long-term sustainability.
b) Ensuring that the Board fulfils its legal obligations in relation to the financial management of a charitable trust.
Governance, Nominations and Remuneration Committee:
a) Reviewing and monitoring the Trust’s governance arrangements for the purpose of ensuring compliance, continuity, sustainability, and enhancing overall performance.
b) Making recommendations to the Board on the appointment and reappointment of Governors.
c) Overseeing the compensation principles and structures across the Trust.
Property Development Committee:
a) Maintaining and developing the Trust’s buildings, utilities, plant and vehicles, grounds, gardens, roadways and security.
b) Developing the Trust’s capital development plan and providing oversight of capital projects.
c) Reviewing and approving the Trust’s 10-year Long Term Maintenance Plan.
d) Overseeing the decarbonisation and sustainability strategy for the Trust.
The Health and Safety Committee is a management committee with a Governor in attendance:
a) Monitoring the health and safety management system, including the development and implementation of health and safety objectives and an improvement plan.
b) Conducting an annual review of Trust Health and Safety performance, in terms of compliance with the Trust’s Health and Safety policies, statutory compliance and best practice.
Nicholas Mercer, BA (Hons) (Chair)
Nick Mercer graduated from the University of London. Nick has over 35 years’ commercial experience, most recently as a Director of Eurostar International. Nick is a Non-Executive Director of two commercial enterprises and he is also the Chair of the Trustees of a charity Clearlyworld.
Stephen Avery, BA, MBA, FCA
Stephen is a graduate of Stirling and Heriot Watt Universities and also studied at the University of Kansas in the USA. He is a Fellow of the Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales and completed his articles with Price Waterhouse. Stephen has held senior financial management roles in a number of organisations and in recent years has worked as a consultant and senior financial management lead for a number of universities in the UK. Stephen has also been a Trustee of a UK Charity and a Director/Governor of a Sixth Form College.
Charles Haywood
Charles Haywood has 40 years experience as a Chartered Quantity Surveyor and Project Manager in the Construction industry. He specialises in risk managing construction projects and has regularly acted as an Expert Witness in resolving disputes. For 20 years he was a director of a local Surveying Practice before more recently taking on a consultancy role. He chaired the Sussex Constructing Excellence Club promoting best practice and driving innovation in the sector.
Gnananandan Janakan (known as Jan), MBBS FRCS MSc
Jan graduated from the University of London and is now a Consultant Surgeon specialising in colorectal cancer and major trauma working at the King's College Hospital, London. In the past he has been the safeguarding governor at a prep school. Jan is also a reserve Royal Air Force Officer working with the Air Cadets.
Sarah Jelly (Safeguarding Governor)
Sarah Jelly is solicitor specialising in Family Law. She is also an accredited family mediator. She has previously been a Governor at another school and is a past parent, having had a daughter in the Senior School.
Gautam Kakar
Gautam has over 25 years of experience in actuarial, financial modelling and risk management in the financial services sector in the UK and Asia.
Jeremy Maynard, MA (Oxon)
Jeremy has over 40 years' business experience, including 25 years as managing director of several food manufacturing companies. He is a trustee of another charity (Rye, Winchelsea & District Memorial Hospital).
Kate Nash, BEd
After 30 years teaching experience in the independent sector, 10 as Head of Pre Prep at Marlborough House School, Kate Nash has worked as a Subject Advisor for IAPS and as a freelance educational consultant; this includes delivering teacher training to the independent sector globally. Kate is also a Governor at another Prep School and she works as a volunteer inter-generational mediator.
Victoria Parker, BSc, MRICS
Victoria holds a degree in Land Management from Reading University and has been a qualified member of the RICS since 1996. Victoria is a member of the Worshipful Company of Constructors, where she also serves as Almoner to the livery company. She recently completed the Cranfield University School of Management 'Business Growth Programme' and continues to be a member of the BGP Board.
Both of Victoria's children attended Bede's Senior School.
Marios Pattihis
Marios Pattihis is a solicitor who has over 40 years experience and he specialises in the commercial property sector.
Giles Perrin
Giles Perrin has over 25 years of experience in UK independent, state and international school settings. He is the son of the Senior School’s founding Headmaster Roger Perrin and his family lived at the Senior School from 1978 – 2003. Giles graduated from Edinburgh University with a BA in Religious Studies and Theology and began his teaching career at the Senior School, initially as a teacher and latterly as the Housemaster of Dicker Knights. Following this Giles worked in the state sector in Frome and then as part of a management team, founding a boarding school in India. In 2010 Giles founded Claremont Senior School, where he was based for 13 years.
Susanna Rynehart
Susanna is an employment solicitor, who has been in private practice for 28 years. She was formerly Chair of Governors in another school and is a Trustee of Mediation Plus, a charitable mediation service in Sussex.
Kyle Siwek, BA MSt
Kyle is a doctoral student at the University of Oxford. His research examines the relationship between the Church of England and the British state during the twentieth century. He has previously been a governor of two secondary schools and also a trustee of a Music Education Hub. At Oxford, he is a student representative on his college’s governing body, and is a member of the Humanities Divisional Board. Kyle also has a keen interest in music, and is a Choral Scholar at The Queen’s College, Oxford.
Philippa Southern MA (Oxon), ACA
Philippa graduated from Oxford University and is a member of the ICAEW. After a career at Andersen and Deloitte, she spent six years in Argentina and Denmark. Philippa currently works in special educational needs and is a trustee of another charity.
The Reverend Jeremy Sykes, MA (Hons)
Jeremy Sykes is an Anglican priest and has nearly 30 years’ experience working in a wide range of independent boarding and day schools both prep and senior. He was Chaplain at Giggleswick School and a housemaster, Headmaster of Great Walstead School and more recently Chaplain of Hurstpierpoint College. He is currently Vicar of the parish of Hellingly and Upper Dicker. He is also a foundation governor at a local federation of maintained primary schools.
Alex Targett
Alex is a proud Bede's alumnus who went on to study Economics at the University of Bath. With four years of experience as an independent school consultant, Alex has specialised in using technology to improve school transport systems, with a passion for innovation in education.

History of the Senior School
Founded in 1978 by Mr Peter Pyemont, Bede's Senior School grew out of Bede's Preparatory School in Eastbourne.
Based at the heart of the rural village of Upper Dicker, the School is surrounded by over 100 beautiful acres of Sussex Downs National Park, a site of Special Scientific Interest, in an estate established by Horatio Bottomley, the notorious swindler, MP and founder of the Financial Times.
During Bottomley's heyday, 'The Dicker' (as the School's site is known) included kennels, a stable yard for breeding racehorses and still boasts the lake and stunning gardens landscaped by Bottomley's team of gardeners.
Indeed Berwick, the local train station, was built where it was because Bottomley influenced the decision in parliament; the stop was originally called 'The Dicker Halt' after the estate.
After Horatio Bottomley was jailed for fraud and his estate repossessed, The Dicker went through several owners before being acquired by the newly founded St Bede's School Trust at the end of the 1970s.
Bede's Senior School grew rapidly over the ensuing years, from a starting figure of 23 pupils to today's roll of approximately 750, making Bede's one of the fastest-growing and most successful independent schools of the 20th Century.
A recent major development has been the new Dorms boarding house and in September 2027, a new £6 million development which will extend provision at the Senior School campus, for pupils in Years 7 and 8.
What's happening at Bede's
Pupils at Bede’s School in Sussex are celebrating today after delivering another record-breaking performance, securing the school’s best-ever GCSE results. Just under half (47%) of all grades awarded were at the highest 9–7 level (or equivalent).
Pupils at Bede’s School are celebrating a historic academic milestone today, having achieved the finest A Level and BTEC results in the Sussex school’s history. An impressive 84% of all grades were awarded at A* to B, with a third of all grades (33%) achieved at the top A* level (or equivalent).
Bede’s School is delighted to announce a prestigious new commercial partnership with Premier League club Brighton & Hove Albion FC. This collaboration unites two of the South East’s leading institutions, establishing a strong partnership alignment rooted in shared values, community engagement and focus on developing excellence.

Senior School Entry
Choosing the right school for your child is a profound decision. At Bede’s, we welcome boys and girls who are eager to engage with the world, discover their passions, and thrive in an inclusive, high-achieving environment. Our holistic approach focuses on the individual, prioritising wellbeing and discovery right alongside academic rigour.
We inspire tomorrow’s thinkers, creators and problem solvers.
"Whatever form your visit takes, you will meet our pupils - our greatest asset - and discover from them why Bede's might be the perfect fit."
- Richard Mills, Director of Admissions
Key entry points:
Most students join our campus at one of following main stages, though mid-year transfers are considered if space allows:
Year 7 or 8 Entry (11 or 12+):
Year 9 Entry (13+):
Year 10 Entry (14+):
Sixth Form Entry (16+):
Attending an Open Morning or booking a private tour is the perfect way to feel the energy of our campus. Meet our teachers, explore our 100-acre Sussex countryside grounds, and see our world-class facilities in action.
If you book a private tour you will be shown round by the Registrar or Director of Admissions or one of our students. You will also have the opportunity to meet with a member of the Senior Management Team or specialist staff such as sports coaches or one of the SEN team. If sport is of particular interest we can also try to arrange a taster coaching session so please let us know in advance if this is the case.
If you prefer to attend one of our Open Mornings, you will be shown round by one of our students and there will be talks which cover the academic programme, Sixth Form and sports as well as speeches by the Headmaster and our students.
When you are ready, create an account on our secure online admissions portal. You will need to upload a copy of your child's passport, a recent photo, and their latest school report, alongside a non-refundable registration fee.
For Year 7, 8 and 9 entry, applicants are invited to a 'Bede’s Experience (BE) Day'. Rather than intense exam rooms, children join small groups to take part in dynamic team tasks, casual group discussions, an individual chat, and a computer-based assessment. For Sixth Form entry, a formal interview with senior staff and a review of predicted GCSE grades are required.
We typically write to families within two weeks of their assessment day. Offers for Year 9 are unconditional, giving you absolute peace of mind for the final years of prep school, while Sixth Form offers are conditional on GCSE outcomes.

How to visit us:
Open Morning
A wonderful and relaxed way to get a first look. You can enjoy a pupil-led tour, hear a short talk from the Headmaster and other specialist staff, and get the chance to chat informally with everyone from faculty heads to sports coaches.
Personal Tours
If you prefer a more tailored experience, you can book a private tour on a normal working day with one of our pupils followed by a member of our senior team or a specialist within the school, such as a sports coach or performing arts lead.
Learn more about what life is like for our Senior School pupils

Pre-School
Children move into the Pre-School during the last year of their time at Bede’s Nursery and in preparation for the transition into Reception, the focus is very much on promoting independence.
Growing Independence
Upon transition to the Pre-School class, the children work together, to follow our five ‘Golden Rules’, for example, good sharing, listening to one another, good manners and of course kindness. These are embedded into the curriculum and implemented throughout all of nursery life.
We encourage the children to ‘have a go’ whilst maintaining a positive, caring and supportive environment. Positive reinforcement, alongside close links and communication with parents helps us embed these codes of behaviour and expectations.
Beyond the Nursery
With both Holywell and Bede’s Prep School’s facilities open to them, the Nursery children have full access to the Bede’s Prep School Swimming Pool, Library, Music Centre and Sports Hall, and they also eat in the Bede’s Prep Dining Hall, overlooking the sea. The Pre-School children also have the opportunity to catch the bus to School if parents wish them to.
Our Reception teacher also has regular sessions with the Pre-School children to enhance their development and support their transition into Reception. We see a huge change in each child’s independence and learning during their time in Holywell, with every individual developing bags of confidence, firm friendships and plenty of new skills and knowledge.
We also organise termly trips, including trips to Friston Forest and the Downs, the theatre as well as our fortnightly Beach School. We regularly welcome visitors to the school including theatre companies, pupils from the Senior School, scientists from Herstmonceux Planetarium and many more.

Academic Programme
We believe pupils perform at their best when they feel happy, valued, and inspired. Our First Year curriculum allows pupils to deepen their talents while equipping them with the future-ready skills needed for modern careers.
We inspire critical thinkers and problem solvers.
Academic Breadth
To ensure strong academic footing, 13.5 hours are ring-fenced for core subjects - English, Maths, Science, and Languages. Around this, pupils tailor their learning: those who excel in Music, Dance, or Art can focus intensely on creative development, while others choose additional academic subjects.
Broadening their horizons further, The World carousel offers an exciting introduction to politics, philosophy, history, and geography, while the Twenty-First Century carousel develops both practical abilities (cookery, first aid) and essential interpersonal skills.
Future Preparation
Supported by a vibrant co-curricular programme and a Term 1 Peak District Outdoor Pursuits week, pupils build confidence and strong peer connections. By Term 2, with close support from their Personal Tutor, each child is perfectly placed to select their GCSE, IGCSE, and BTEC pathways for the Fifth Form.

Pastoral
The pastoral system at Bede’s Senior School is designed around a holistic, "school within a school" structure that prioritises individual care, personal development, and active pupil involvement.
At Bede’s, wellbeing and ambition thrive side by side.
The House System
At the core of Bede’s pastoral care are its ten Day and Boarding Houses. Operating as close-knit communities, each House is led by a Housemaster or Housemistress, supported by Deputy Heads, Resident or Personal Tutors who oversee small groups of 10–12 pupils, meeting with them daily for one-to-one mentoring and academic oversight. This close oversight ensures every student is known individually, while inter-House competitions—ranging from House Music to sports - foster a strong sense of belonging, team spirit, and healthy rivalry.
Learn more about our House System >
Health and Wellbeing
Bede’s takes a proactive approach to physical and emotional health through its dedicated Health and Wellbeing Centre. Operating on an "open door" policy, the centre provides professional first aid, medical clinics with visiting GPs, and ongoing support for physical health. Recognizing the vital importance of mental health, the school offers free, confidential counselling led by qualified BACP-accredited counsellors. The pastoral team collaborates continuously to ensure wrap-around emotional care, offering students a safe space to navigate challenges.
Pupil Voice
Bede’s strongly emphasises empowering students to shape their own school community. Pupil voice is driven through structured House Councils and a rigorous, pupil-led Prefect body. Prefects serve as crucial role models, organizing charity initiatives and chairing student committees that directly connect the Senior Leadership Team with the wider student body. Through these platforms, pupils actively lead initiatives on important social topics such as mental health awareness, gender equality, and diversity, ensuring student perspectives actively influence school life.
By seamlessly blending structured House mentoring, professional wellbeing support, and meaningful pupil leadership, Bede’s creates a nurturing environment where every student can flourish.
